description: Geographic bin map of 19 Australian National Surfing Reserves, grouped into fixed 2-degree by 2-degree cells; counts are not coastline-normalised.

usermeta.title: Where Do Recognised Surfing Reserves Cluster?
usermeta.annotation: Six reserves fall within the Sydney–Central Coast 2° cell: the largest cluster, accounting for 32% of all 19 listings.
usermeta.analysis: Grouping the 19 National Surfing Reserves into fixed 2° longitude × 2° latitude grid cells produces ten occupied cells. The strongest concentration is the Sydney–Central Coast cell (150°–152°E; 34°–32°S), containing six reserves: Maroubra, Bondi, North Narrabeen, Manly–Freshwater, Merewether and Norah Head. They represent 32% of all listed reserves. Another cell near the NSW–Queensland border groups three sites—Lennox Head, Angourie and Gold Coast—while Margaret River and Yallingup share a cell in southwest WA. Other reserves, including Kalbarri, Noosa and Phillip Island, lie in separate cells. This highlights the concentration of formal heritage recognition along parts of the east coast, alongside isolated locations elsewhere. The cells are equal in degrees rather than kilometres squared; they may include ocean and differ in coastline length. The chart therefore counts listed reserves per cell, not surf quality, surfer numbers or a coastline-normalised density.
